messages:
marta: quick heads-up — ran a targeted profiler on paged-attn with the new eviction heuristic (age+reuse) and smaller blocks (6KB). results show a sharp compaction CPU spike and repeated device syncs around 12:22. flame graphs attached but summary below.

devon: ugh. did you also see kernsel fallback churn? last week that was our primary perf regression.

marta: yes — kernsel occasionally falls back to the generic path for long seqs after eviction storms. saw logs like `kernsel: fallback aten_attn_longseq` around the same window.

liam: can you paste the config you used?

marta: sure — minimal diff from prod: 
```yaml
block_manager:
  block_size: 6144  # bytes
  compaction_trigger: 0.6
  reuse_window_ms: 120000
allocator:
  split_merge: true
  min_free_frag: 65536  # bytes
  aggressive_coalesce: false
batching:
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  latency_slo_ms: 60
```

kai: interesting. lowering block_size reduced internal waste but increased the frequency of compaction runs. compaction cost is nontrivial because we call `cudaDeviceSynchronize()` in the hot path to ensure workspace consistency.

devon: that sync is the killer. do we still need a full sync for compaction, or can we move to an async mark-and-prepare?

marta: follow-up experiment idea: 1) bump block_size -> 16KB and keep reuse_window same; 2) keep 6KB but increase reuse_window to 10m; 3) try deferred compaction (mark-only, then background stitch). measurement targets: compaction time, # kernsel fallback events, p99 latency, OOMs per hour.

liam: i'll run A/B microbench with 1M token trace and prioritized KV cache hits. expected runtime ~30m per variant. i'll collect `nvprof` summaries + our flamegraphs.

kai: also add a run that disables `split_merge` in allocator — merger logic may be causing transient fragmentation under small-block regime.

marta: good call. initial numbers (6KB baseline): compaction runs ~0.7s avg, compaction CPU ~= 15% of runtime, kernsel fallback spikes from 0 to ~3 events per 10k requests, p99 latency +18%. memory overhead dropped by ~6%.

devon: tradeoff looks classic: smaller blocks -> less steady-state waste but more compaction churn and increased kernel fallback (so worse latency).

liam: preliminary patch i'm going to test: bump default block_size to 12KB, keep `split_merge: true`, and add a non-blocking compaction path that defers device sync until idle. i'll post results.

infra-bot: perf-run queued: id=perf-20240211-010, variants=4, estimated-completion=35m.

marta: can we also instrument KV cache eviction patterns? I'm curious whether hot prefixes are being evicted and rehydrated quickly causing repeat KVC loads.

kai: yes — add `kv.eviction_trace=true` to runs. also log prefix reuse count per block.

devon: if deferring sync helps, we might be able to avoid kernsel fallback entirely for most traces. otherwise consider a tiny fast-path kernel for 6-12KB blocks to reduce fallbacks.

marta: agreed. action items: 
- liam: run the four variants + post nvprof + flamegraphs (ETA ~1h).
- kai: add kv eviction tracing and header for reuse counts.
- devon: prototype a micro kernel path for small-block attention if fallback persists.
- marta: collate results and recommend default block_size + compaction policy.

liam: starting perf-run now. i'll upload artifacts to the perf bucket under `runs/1749873210/`. ping when done. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

marta: thanks — if initial run shows >10% p99 regression we revert the 6KB experiment in canary. :thumbsup:
